Title
Software Engineer - Real-Time Geospatial Mapping for Planetary Exploration
BELONG. CONNECT. GROW. with KBR.
Around here, we define the future. We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.
Description Of Work Effort
Join NASA Ames writing software to help explore the moon! Help us meet the emerging needs of Artemis, Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) and future Moon-to-Mars missions. Looking for a software engineer to assist with development of two coordinated work efforts:
M2M CSDS - the Moon to Mars Collaborative Science Data System
WITME - Web-Based Integrated Terrain Model Estimation tool
These tools provide a reusable, science-centric collaboration platform that enables distributed science teams to collectively visualize, analyze, and interpret mission data in support of time-critical decision making. They will prototype capability for uncertainty-aware fusion of orbital and surface terrain data for real-time operational decision support.
M2M CSDS and WITME both build on NASA Ames - developed collaborative data systems and science operations architectures matured through the Exploration Ground Data Systems (xGDS) research project and VIPER mission science operations.
M2M CSDS development will require the applicant to work closely with an active CLPS science team to populate the proof-of-concept M2M CSDS with mission relevant data. Software development will include an interactive, shared planning/replanning and execution monitoring capability that builds on design concepts developed for the Ames-led xGDS in a mature mission-proven environment. The work effort will include the integration of FedRAMP and NASA approved AI tools (e.g. Google Gemini) to provide summarization and search capabilities on the data sets and annotations deployed in M2M CSDS. These capabilities are anticipated to provide substantial benefits for supporting real-time science and operations (e.g. rapid initial generation of shift handover highlights that can be further augmented and edited by science team members).
WITME involves the development and application of statistically principled fusion methods to weight orbital and surface data by their uncertainties, and build unified 3D models with quantitative confidence estimates derived from these data. Specifically, the applicant will help develop effective user interfaces and displays to communicate confidence in terrain model data at different locations. This will enable mission teams to rapidly assimilate new terrain data, improving traverse planning and decision-making through a collaborative web-based interface.

Description
AWS CloudWatch OpenTelemetry is hiring!
Come build the next generation of cloud observability with us. Amazon CloudWatch gives every AWS customer a single platform to send, store, and query metrics from over 70 AWS services alongside their own application telemetry, using the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) and Prometheus Query Language (PromQL). Our Seattle team owns the query execution and long-term metrics storage systems that make this possible: the distributed query engine that evaluates PromQL expressions in real time, the storage access layer that serves reads across storage tiers, and the durable pipeline that compacts and indexes billions metric data points per day and keeps them queryable for up to 15 months. We serve customers who depend on CloudWatch to monitor production systems using Grafana, Prometheus, and other Prometheus-compatible tools. The Seattle team is small, early, and still making the foundational architecture decisions that will shape this service for years. Engineers who join now will have a visible and lasting influence on what it becomes. Engineers who thrive here pair strong distributed systems instincts with the discipline to build for correctness and availability at AWS scale.
Key job responsibilities
Design, implement, and test new features across our distributed query and long-term metrics storage systems using Rust and Java, leveraging AWS services including S3, Kinesis, DynamoDB, and ECS.
Operate and maintain a globally available 24x7 service that customers rely on to monitor, alert, and analyze their metrics in real time, identifying root causes of operational issues and applying permanent fixes.
Collaborate with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand requirements, influence our roadmap, and shape how millions of developers and SREs monitor their systems.
Contribute to the full software development lifecycle — from design and code reviews to testing, deployment, and documentation — while mentoring teammates through constructive feedback.
Evaluate new tools and approaches to keep our systems and practices current, making recommendations to the team on adoption and integration.
A day in the life
On a typical day you might root-cause a customer query issue, release a new feature, consult with principal engineers on a hard architectural tradeoff, or design a solution to a storage or performance challenge you have never seen before. You translate customer requirements into designs, evaluate tradeoffs, and break work into incremental deliverables your team can ship. A strong community of principal and senior engineers gives direct feedback and pushes your thinking. You are surrounded by people who are passionate about observability and who believe there is still a lot of ground to cover in helping developers, SREs, and operators understand their systems.
About The Team
The AWS CloudWatch OpenTelemetry team builds the query execution and long-term metrics storage systems behind Amazon CloudWatch. We are a small, early-stage team in Seattle making foundational architecture decisions that will shape this service for years. Our mission is to give every AWS customer a reliable, performant way to store, query, and act on their metrics using open standards like OTLP and PromQL.
We invest in growing our engineers from day one — you will be paired with a buddy, work closely with senior and principal engineers, and build a personalized development plan with your manager. Our culture values knowledge sharing, constructive feedback, and an inclusive environment where every voice is heard.

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Experience with server, storage, networking, or large-scale distributed systems
Experience leading the design, build and deployment of complex and performant (reliable and scalable) software solutions in production
Familiarity with time-series data, metrics systems, or the Prometheus and OpenTelemetry ecosystems
Experience with S3-based storage, stream processing (e.g., Kinesis, Kafka), or columnar storage formats such as Parquet
Familiarity with PromQL or other query languages for time-series data
Experience with query planning, storage compaction, or performance optimization at scale

Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests as a normal part of every change.
Debug failures across the stack — from an API response, through service code and workflow orchestration, down to a Kubernetes cluster.

Working knowledge of SQL and relational data modeling.
Comfort with Git, the command line, and Linux.
Evidence of self-driven building — internships, personal projects, open-source contributions, hackathons, or coursework you took further than the assignment required.
Clear written communication; able to explain a problem and a proposed fix in text to a distributed team.
Genuine curiosity about infrastructure, distributed systems, and how large-scale platforms are built.

Something you built and can walk us through in detail: what it does, why you designed it that way, and what you would change now.
Willingness to be reviewed rigorously and to treat feedback as the fastest way to get better.
Testing instinct — you can explain how you know your own code works.
Authorization to work in the United States.
Nice to Have
Exposure to Go in a project, internship, or coursework.
Familiarity with containers and Kubernetes (docker, kubectl, Helm) at any depth.
Cloud experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Any experience with REST API design, OpenAPI, or client SDKs.
Exposure to CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions or equivalent).
Interest in or coursework on AI/ML infrastructure, GPU computing, or distributed systems.

Open-source contributions of any size — issues, docs, and small fixes all count.
Security or systems-programming coursework, CTF participation, or similar.
Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science & Engineering or related field or 6months to 1 year related experience.

Work with an established Silicon Valley leader in the cloud infrastructure industry;
Work with exceptionally passionate, talented and engaging colleagues, helping Fortune 500 and Global 2000 customers implement next-generation cloud technologies;
Be a part of cutting-edge, open-source innovation;
Thrive in the high-energy environment of a young company where openness, collaboration, risk-taking, and continuous growth are valued;
Professional development and training;
Attend conferences and working groups;
Company outings, happy hours, hackathons, and tech talks;
Receive a competitive compensation package with a strong benefits plan.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for the world’s best engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.
As Starlink grows to serve billions of users around the world, we’re continuously assessing ways to maximize the use of our technology for people around the world. Our CDN team will be pivotal in this effort, building scalable distributed systems that underly the future offerings Starlink is able to provide to users and customers around the world.

Design, build, and scale a new Content Delivery Network (CDN) for Starlink
Build robust, responsive, and scalable distributed systems.
Build the necessary tools, visibility, and alerting mechanisms to effectively diagnose, operate, and maintain complex, business-critical systems in real-time.
Design algorithms to understand and optimize hardware utilization and cost efficiency, evaluated against intuitive and business-critical performance metrics.

Participate in and lead architecture, design, and code reviews.

Advanced degree in computer science or engineering.

Professional experience designing, building, and/ scaling a CDN system.

SUMMARY:
The DevOps Release Engineer will take ownership of code review, release management, and production deployments across our enterprise application environment, while also building out the tooling and processes that make the pipeline more reliable and efficient over time.
This position serves as the checkpoint between development and production; reviewing code changes, coordinating and executing releases, and maintaining the health of our source control and deployment processes. The role works closely with our programming team and IT leadership and has no direct reports.
Beyond day-to-day release management, this is an opportunity to modernize how we build, test, and deploy changes – introducing automation, standardized branching and release procedures, and improved tooling where gaps exist.
The role also owns environment management. Keeping our development, test, and production environments current, consistent with one another, and ready for the team to use is a core responsibility. Equally important is communication: this person is a direct point of contact for the business and application leadership who sponsor the changes being released, and is expected to clearly tell them what is going out, when, what changed, and what to expect.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
·        Review code changes submitted by the development team for quality, completeness, and adherence to established coding standards prior to merge.
·        Manage and execute the promotion of code changes from development through testing and into production across our COBOL, C#.NET/WinForms, and SQL Server environments.
·        Administer and maintain our Bitbucket repositories, including branching strategy, permissions, merge policies, and repository health.
·        Support developers using TortoiseGit and Bitbucket in their day-to-day version control workflows.
·        Own environment management across development, test, and production – ensuring environments are current, consistent with one another, refreshed on a known schedule, and documented.
·        Keep non-production environments aligned with production, including code levels, database schema and reference data, configuration, and integration endpoints.
·        Coordinate release schedules and deployment windows with the development team and business stakeholders to minimize disruption.
·        Communicate release schedules and development windows with the development team and business stakeholders to minimize disruption.
·        Communicate release plans, schedules, contents, and outcomes to application owners and company leadership in language that a non-technical stakeholder can act on.
·        Provide clear, timely communication when a deployment encounters problems, including business impact, current status, and expected resolution.
·        Maintain and improve build, deployment, and rollback procedures, including documentation of current processes.
·        Identify gaps in our current deployment and release tooling and propose, build, and implement improvements (for example, automation scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment checklists).
·        Monitor deployments for issues and coordinate rollback or remediation when necessary.
·        Maintain change logs, release notes, and deployment records for audit and troubleshooting purposes.
·        Partner with the Senior Technical Project Manager and development team to align release timing with project milestones.
·        Perform scheduled releases outside of standard business hours, including occasional evenings and weekends, and respond when a deployment issue requires attention.
·        Must work on-site in Fairfield, OH, one or more days a week to meet the demands of the position and business needs.
TECHNOLOGY ENVIRONMENT:
Quality Gold’s application environment supports manufacturing, inventory, purchasing, pricing, order processing, fulfillment, shipping, accounting, reporting, and external business partners. It includes:
·        Bitbucket for source control, with TortoiseGit as the primary client for developers.
·        C#.NET/WinForms applications.
·        Microsoft SQL Server.
·        Long-standing COBOL-based legacy systems.
·        A largely manual release and deployment process, with meaningful room to introduce modern automation and tooling.
·        Separate development, test, and production environments that are currently maintained and refreshed manually.
This is a hands-on technical role.
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:
This position has no direct supervisory responsibilities.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
GNC ENGINEER, FLEET MANAGEMENT (STARSHIELD)
Starshield leverages SpaceX’s Starlink technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While Starlink is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is designed for government use, with an initial focus on earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads.
As an engineer on the GNC (Guidance, Navigation, and Control), Fleet Management team, you will be responsible for the complete lifecycle of Starshield's constellation. The Fleet Management team designs the constellation through analysis and simulation, and then brings it into reality through satellite and ground software development. This is an opportunity to apply expertise in orbital mechanics to both define constellation geometry and implement the control systems necessary to maintain it (including orbit raise, station keeping, and collision avoidance algorithms). This all requires working collaboratively across engineering teams to represent the satellite system at the constellation level, ultimately defining scope and requirements for future vehicles.
Responsibilities
Develop highly reliable and performant GNC algorithms, flight software, simulations, tools, services, and dashboards using C++ or Python
Participate in architecture, design, and code reviews
Constellation design and network-level analysis of both existing and proposed systems
Bulk analysis to review performance data from various elements of the Starshield constellation and hosted payloads
Write high-quality technical documentation of programs, algorithms, or analysis
Support your relevant on-call operations rotation, commanding satellites or reviewing data to keep our vehicles, payloads, and networks continuously operating at peak performance

Bachelor's degree in computer science, aerospace, physics, or an engineering discipline
Software development experience in either C++ or Python
Preferred Skills And Experience
Master's degree or Ph.D. in an engineering discipline, computer science, or physics
Experience developing, debugging, and deploying software that has been used in real-world applications/projects
Creative approach to problem-solving, exceptional analytical skills, and engineering fundamentals
Familiarity with numerical probability of collision methods such as Alfano, Foster, and Hall
Experience with automating complex systems
Strong understanding of orbital mechanics, including low thrust trajectory optimization and station-keeping
Experience in verifying GNC algorithm performance via simulation, and validation of the simulation's models
Experience with space-based sensor platforms and state estimation, particularly attitude determination, orbit determination, GNSS, and radio navigation
General familiarity with the disciplines necessary for spacecraft flight including; structures, propulsion, avionics, GNC, flight software, dynamics, launch and mission operations, and integration. Practical experience in real-world development of these systems is highly desired.
Capable of identifying and solving complex problems with little to no supervision or direction
Passion for advancing the commercial space industry
Ability to work in a fast-paced, autonomously driven, and demanding start-up atmosphere
Excellent communication skills both written and verbal
Active Top Secret, Top Secret SCI, or DOE Level Q clearance, or the ability to obtain and maintain one
Additional Requirements
Able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical path development and/or critical on-orbit operations
An active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions; if so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol test
Pay Range
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
GNC Engineer/Level I: $125,000.00 - $150,000.00/per year

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. Charity Navigator is the world's largest and most-utilized independent nonprofit evaluator. The Role
You will build and ship production LLM-powered and agentic features that make 2.4 million nonprofit profiles easier to search, compare, and understand - so a donor gets a clear answer instead of a spreadsheet.
This is application-layer work. You will partner with our existing engineering team rather than owning the pipelines yourself, so your time goes into the AI features people use.
You will report to the VP of Engineering and work closely with them and other senior engineers on system design, technical direction, and strategic AI opportunities. You will own AI features from day one, with regular design review and hands-on guidance on the harder architectural calls, and take on more architectural ownership as you build depth in production AI systems.

Build and ship production LLM-powered and agentic features - prompt orchestration, tool calling, embeddings, structured outputs - favoring reusable components over one-off solutions.

development experience.

Resourcefulness and adaptability.

Familiarity with relational databases and SQL, and a basic mental model of how a web request becomes a database query
You use AI coding tools and you've formed opinions about them — including where they mislead you and how you catch it

About BusRight
More than 26 million students ride approximately 500,000 school buses every day.
At BusRight, we are building the modern operating system for school transportation, helping districts manage routing, driver navigation, live GPS tracking, student transportation data, and communication with families.
We are looking for a Technical Support Engineer who enjoys understanding complex systems, debugging production issues, writing code, and building tools that make both our product and our teams more effective.
The Role
This is a hands on technical engineering role focused on investigating real world system behavior and building solutions.
You will work across our application, APIs, logs, data integrations, GPS systems, hardware, and codebase to understand how things work and why they sometimes do not.
A meaningful part of the role involves writing, improving, and maintaining TypeScript and JavaScript scripts and internal tools. These may help investigate production behavior, analyze customer data, automate operational workflows, validate integrations, or provide functionality that does not yet exist in the product.
You will also own complex customer reported issues from investigation through resolution, working directly with Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers when needed.
What You Will Do
• Investigate complex production issues across application behavior, APIs, logs, integrations, data, GPS, and hardware
• Read and understand existing TypeScript and JavaScript code to trace system behavior and identify root causes
• Write new TypeScript and JavaScript scripts to solve technical and operational problems
• Maintain and improve existing internal scripts and tools as requirements and systems evolve
• Build custom tooling for data analysis, troubleshooting, validation, reporting, and internal workflows
• Work with APIs and large datasets to investigate issues and build solutions
• Reproduce bugs and provide Engineering with clear technical findings, evidence, and recommended next steps
• Troubleshoot Student Information System integrations and data synchronization issues
• Investigate GPS, tablet, connectivity, and other deployed hardware behavior
• Identify repetitive work and replace it with automation, tooling, or better internal systems
• Use AI assisted workflows to accelerate coding, debugging, investigation, and technical problem solving
• Own complex customer reported issues through resolution and ensure technical problems do not get lost between teams
What We Are Looking For
• 2+ years of experience in support engineering, software engineering, solutions engineering, technical support, or a similar technical role
• Strong TypeScript or JavaScript experience, including the ability to understand existing code and write new scripts independently
• Experience debugging software and investigating production system behavior
• Experience working with APIs, logs, backend systems, integrations, and structured data
• Comfortable building internal tools and scripts to solve problems that do not have an existing solution
• Comfortable maintaining code and tooling after the initial solution is built
• Experience analyzing data using SQL, spreadsheets, scripts, or similar tools
• Strong analytical skills and the ability to break ambiguous problems into smaller technical questions
• Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical findings clearly
• A strong sense of ownership and willingness to drive problems through resolution
• Comfortable working in a fast moving environment where you may need to design the solution rather than follow an existing process
• Experience with or strong interest in using AI as part of everyday engineering work
Why This Role
You will work on problems that span software, data, integrations, GPS, hardware, and real world transportation operations.
One day you might trace an issue through logs and APIs. Another day you might write a TypeScript script to analyze thousands of records, build an internal tool to automate a workflow, or investigate behavior across the application and deployed hardware.
You will work directly with engineers, have access to the systems and data needed to investigate problems deeply, and build solutions when existing product functionality is not enough.
You will not just identify problems. You will understand them, solve them, and build tools that make the next problem easier to solve.

Deliver production-quality, GxP-aligned code using strong practices in testing, computer system validation (CSV/CSA), CI/CD, logging, audit trails, versioning, and documentation suitable for regulatory inspection.

Backed by some of the top venture capital firms in Silicon Valley and founded by third-time founders with two successful exits, Levelpath is building autonomous procurement.

You will be on calls with customer IT and integration teams, whiteboarding data flows, debugging auth handshakes live, and turning ambiguous requirements into working pipelines. When a customer's integration engineer is stuck, you are the person who gets them moving again.
You will build with our agentic software factory, and you will improve it. The factory is optimized for exactly this work: well-specified contracts and a premium on verification. It is not perfect, and when it falls short you fix the cause, contributing tooling back so the next integration ships faster. Agents are the execution capacity here. Your job is to drive them to the outcome: unblock them when they stall, correct them when they drift, and verify what they ship.
You will also be the engineering presence in the US timezone. Our core platform team is distributed internationally, and you help anchor US-hours on-call coverage so customers get a fast, expert response no matter when things break. On-call is a real part of this role, and we invest in the observability, runbooks, and agent tooling that make it sane.

Real experience with third-party APIs and integration work: REST and GraphQL, webhooks, OAuth and SAML flows, data mapping, and the patience to read someone else's API docs carefully.
AI-pilled, genuinely. Your instinct is to hand work to agents first, and you want to turn over as much as possible to AI, in your own workflow and in the product. You have the judgment to know when it worked.
A deep-seated need to ship. We believe we win by outshipping everyone, and we hire engineers who treat blockers as things to bulldoze, not things to wait on.

Who We Are
Serval is an AI-native automation platform transforming how enterprises operate. We build intelligent agents that understand real-world workflows and execute them end-to-end — replacing manual processes and rigid legacy systems with adaptive, learning software. Founded in early 2024, Serval is already trusted by companies like Fox, Notion, Perplexity, Vercel, and Brex to automate high-volume, high-friction operational work across their organizations.
At the core of Serval is an agentic AI platform that turns natural language into production-grade workflows. Our agents don’t just respond to requests — they reason, take action across systems, and continuously improve with usage. What began with operational use cases has quickly evolved into a horizontal AI automation layer used across IT, HR, Finance, Security, Legal, and Engineering.
Our mission is to eliminate repetitive, manual work across the enterprise and give teams leverage through intelligent automation. Long term, we’re building the universal AI operations layer — a system of agents that sits across business functions and runs the workflows that keep modern companies moving.
We’re backed by leading investors including Sequoia Capital, Redpoint Ventures, Meritech, First Round, General Catalyst, Elad Gil, and others.
Role Overview
With Serval, an automation that used to take a SOW and a quarter now takes a sentence and an afternoon. That one change is why Automation Engineering is becoming the operating model for enterprise services, and why service teams stop being a bottleneck and start being an advantage.
As an Automation Engineer, you build Serval's agents directly into the customer's instance, and the tickets stop arriving: onboarding, access requests, approvals, the long tail that clogs a service desk. You'll push Serval past its current limits into new use cases, dogfood unreleased features, bring field ideas back to our product team, and act as a practitioner evangelist for both Serval and Automation Engineering.
This is a title we are coining. Nobody has ten years of it yet, so what you build becomes the standard for everyone after you.
What You’ll Do
Build in the platform: design and build automations and AI agents inside customers' Serval instances, from onboarding and access requests to the long tail that clogs a service desk.
Wire up the stack: integrate Serval with customer systems (Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, ServiceNow, Workday) so automations complete end to end.
Run working sessions: embed with IT, HR, Finance, and Legal teams, pull the real process out of them, and turn it into something buildable the same day.
Enable customer builders: turn what you build into reusable patterns and teach customers' own teams to extend them, so adoption compounds after you leave.
Partner with Deployment: work alongside Deployment Strategists to hit the milestones a customer signed up for, and surface risk early when a use case is going sideways.
What You’ll Need
Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.
2+ years in a relevant role (IT or service operations, professional services, solutions engineering, business systems, technical support).
Working knowledge of APIs and REST, JSON, and IAM concepts including SSO, SCIM, and provisioning.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to run a working session, challenge a requirement, and translate technical tradeoffs for non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to learn unfamiliar software quickly and work independently across several customer accounts.
Nice to Have
Experience in an early-stage startup environment.
Hands-on time administering or migrating an ITSM platform (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Freshservice, Zendesk).
Familiarity with IT, security, service management, or workflow automation.
What we offer
Impact: Be a key player in shaping the success of our product and company.
Growth: Build a fundamentally new AI product offering with the support of our experienced team and investors. Grow rapidly with the company.
Culture: Join a culture that values innovation, ownership, accountability, and fun.

**Location:** Oklahoma City, OK, Hybrid
**Schedule:** Monday-Friday, 20 hours per week

**Pay Rate:** Up to $66/hr, with flexibility for the right candidate
## Job Overview
We are seeking an experienced **AS400 Developer/Admin** to support and maintain core IBM AS/400 (IBM i Series) applications. This role will focus on legacy application development, application support, DB2 database management, application-level administration, and coordination with an external hosting provider for environment-related activities.
The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on experience with RPG, RPGLE, CL, DB2 for i, SQL, IBM i administration, and legacy application support.
## Key Responsibilities
* Maintain, modify, troubleshoot, and optimize legacy applications written in RPG, RPG III, RPG IV (ILE RPG), RPGLE, and Control Language (CL).
* Investigate and resolve application bugs, batch processing issues, and user-reported system problems.
* Update existing application logic to support regulatory, licensing, and business process changes.
* Coordinate with external hosting providers regarding system maintenance, OS patching schedules, database utilities, and environment modifications.
* Manage application-level security configurations, user profiles, and object-level authority.
* Review system audit logs, including QAUDJRN, to help maintain system integrity.
* Manage local job queues, active subsystems, and application-level job scheduling.
* Coordinate backup windows, disaster recovery testing, and restoration verification with hosting and infrastructure teams.
* Query, manage, and tune DB2 for i databases.
* Optimize SQL queries and indexes to improve database performance.
* Support automated FTP/SFTP file transfers and integrations with external systems.
* Assist with extracting, cleaning, and archiving legacy data.
* Document application flows, database schemas, legacy business logic, and system interdependencies.
* Support ongoing modernization, data archiving, and migration initiatives.
## Required Qualifications
* Minimum **5 years of hands-on AS400, IBM i, or iSeries application development and support experience**.
* Strong proficiency in **RPG IV, ILE RPG, RPGLE, CL, and SQL**.
* Strong experience with **DB2 for i**.
* Experience working in a **hosted or managed AS400/IBM i environment**.
* Experience coordinating with external hosting or infrastructure providers.
* Experience with IBM i work management, subsystem coordination, application security, and user profile management.
* Strong experience with **FTP/SFTP** and external system integrations.
* Strong troubleshooting and legacy application maintenance experience.
## Preferred Qualifications
* Experience supporting legacy-to-cloud migration initiatives.
* Experience with data extraction, data warehousing, or legacy data archiving.
* Familiarity with **Rational Developer for i (RDi)**.
* Experience supporting public sector or insurance-related systems.
* Experience documenting legacy business logic and system dependencies.
## Work Arrangement
This is a **hybrid contract position based in Oklahoma City, OK**. Candidates should be local to the area or willing to relocate to support required onsite work.

Nearly every company in the world runs on custom software for critical operations like tracking performance metrics, handling support workflows, building admin dashboards, and countless processes you might never have thought of. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.
What You’ll Do
Applications Engineering, part of CoreWeave’s Data Infrastructure organization, builds the software CoreWeave uses to plan and operate its own infrastructure business. Some of that is UNION, our data platform, where anyone in the company can query the lakehouse in plain language and stand up their own dashboards, applications, and agents. The rest is the applications behind decisions like which data centers get which hardware and when, for a company adding gigawatts of capacity a year. Engineering, finance, supply chain, and data center operations all depend on what we ship.
About The Role
You will build full-stack applications, and features in UNION itself, and own all of it in production, from the interface down to the data model. Our stack is TypeScript with React and Next.js, Python services running on Kubernetes, and Postgres alongside the lakehouse. We care more that you have built and run this kind of software than which frameworks you built it in. A good share of the work is AI-facing, meaning natural language interfaces and agents that operate on governed data, plus the evaluation work that tells you whether they are any good. Owning a product area here means you sit with the people who run the process and work out with them what the software should do. You are also the one who answers for it when it breaks. Most of these processes have never been written down anywhere, so a fair amount of the job is working out what to build before you build it.
Who You Are
5+ years building and operating production software, including both backend services and modern web frontends
Strong Python and TypeScript, with real experience in React, Next.js, or a comparable modern framework
Experience designing and running HTTP APIs that other services depend on, including timeouts, retries, and keeping writes correct when a call fails partway through
Strong SQL and relational data modeling, including schemas you had to change after they were already live
Experience shipping LLM-backed features to production, including how you measured whether their output was correct
Hands-on experience with containers and deployment tooling such as Docker, Helm, and Kubernetes, and with operating your own services
Experience wiring applications up to data platforms and analytical databases such as Spark, Kafka, StarRocks, or Snowflake
CI/CD, automated testing, observability, and on-call for the software you own
Experience working directly with non-engineers on problems nobody had specified yet, and shipping software they adopted
Preferred
Experience building AI-native applications such as text-to-SQL interfaces, copilots, agents, or automated insight generation
Experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph, and with the tracing and evaluation tooling around them
Experience designing and running distributed systems in cloud-native environments such as Kubernetes
Familiarity with open table formats such as Iceberg, Delta, or Hudi, and with query engines such as StarRocks, Snowflake, or BigQuery
Experience building internal platforms or tools that other teams used to answer their own questions
Background in an operationally heavy domain such as capacity planning, supply chain, or finance
Wondering if you’re a good fit? We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams – even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk.
You want the people using your software to be people you know by name, and you take it personally when it gets in their way

You work well at speed. Priorities here move with the business, and the problems worth solving tend to arrive on short notice
You want to know whether the AI in your product is any good, and you will build the evals to find out
You stand behind what you ship, whether you wrote it or a model helped you write it
Why CoreWeave?
About
At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:
Be Curious at Your Core
Act Like an Owner
Empower Employees
Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
Achieve More Together
We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for take off, the growth opportunities within the organization are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!

We are seeking an application/software engineer with a strong security focus to evaluate, prioritize, and remediate vulnerabilities and compliance findings across custom applications and infrastructure as code (IaC). Working proficiency with Python, SQL, and VB.NET or legacy .NET frameworks.
Experience with AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) or similar IaC tools (Terraform, CloudFormation).
Hands-on experience working in AWS environments, preferably AWS GovCloud.
Experience with AWS security services (GuardDuty, Security Hub, Inspector, Config).

Experience with CI/CD pipeline security integration (Jenkins, GitLab CI, AWS CodePipeline).

Background in both application development and security operations.

About Navflex
At Navflex, we're pioneering the future of logistics automation through cutting-edge AI and robotics. Our autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) are transforming the way goods are loaded and unloaded, enabling plug-and-play solutions that streamline operations and enhance efficiency across the global supply chain for some of the world’s most demanding warehouse environments. Our international, cross‑disciplinary team in the EU and USA pairs robust mechatronics with cutting‑edge navigation and perception to deliver safe, reliable autonomy in real‑world warehouses and yards. Join us in shaping the future of intelligent logistics.
The Role
Our objective is autonomy in unstructured, real-world environments: vehicles that build a rich spatial understanding of their surroundings, reason about how they'll change, and act decisively within them. Progress compounds: fleet data becomes the substrate for world modeling and simulation, which lets us validate new behaviors faster than physical testing alone.
You'll work on problems where evaluation methodology is still evolving, and you'll contribute to shaping it alongside senior team members. We expect you to track the literature, judge what is ready for real hardware, carry results from prototype to validated capability, and work with core software engineering to bring it into production behind clear requirements and acceptance criteria. Staying current is part of the job, not something you do on your own time.
This is research and development, not research alone. We work on open problems, but always against a product roadmap, and a result counts when it reaches a vehicle and changes something a customer experiences. We move quickly, and nobody here disappears into a lab.
Focus Area: Spatial AI
Perception already runs on our vehicles across LiDAR, depth cameras, inertial sensing, and wheel odometry. You'll deepen its understanding: improve the accuracy and robustness of today's models, harden them against the conditions that degrade performance, and decide what should replace them.
The larger goal is a probabilistic 3D representation of the vehicle's surroundings that holds up over time: persisting through occlusion, decaying honestly when the world may have changed since it was last seen, and carrying calibrated uncertainty the rest of the stack can rely on. Warehouses are dynamic: pallets, people, and other vehicles move while unobserved. How it's encoded is an open question you'll help answer.
The same work extends into state estimation, where learned components complement the classical stack our autonomy team maintains: visual odometry, degeneracy prediction in geometrically weak environments, and pose uncertainty that's trustworthy rather than optimistic.

Models you build run on production vehicles, with field behavior backed by evaluation developed in partnership with the team, with your own contributions clearly reflected in the results
Capabilities you prototype reach production because you contribute clear, well-documented work that the team can build against
You help evaluate external methods and contribute to team discussions on what's worth pursuing

Train, evaluate, and iterate on models using real fleet data: logs, rosbags, and multi-modal sensor streams from vehicles in production
Build and maintain the 3D representation the rest of the stack consumes, with the calibration and sensor health monitoring it depends on
Contribute to baselines and evaluation methodology, applying and refining standards set by the team

These system-level processes integrate sensors, actuators, mechanisms, controls, computer, electrical, and human interactions to deliver systems that meet and exceed customer, safety, regulatory, and business requirements. This is done through the execution of test plans, documentation of test results, defect tracking and triage, automation of repetitive test tasks, and presenting results, feedback, and recommendations to cross-functional teams and stakeholders.

Train new team members on team procedures and test methodologies

You might start your morning executing a functional test plan on a newly deployed packaging system, documenting pass/fail results against defined KPIs. Mid-morning, you could be triaging defects from overnight testing, isolating bugs, and providing detailed reproduction steps to hardware engineers. In the afternoon, you might be writing automation scripts to streamline repetitive data collection tasks, or collaborating with controls engineers to verify safety interlock functionality. Our work spans the entire product development lifecycle—from early concept validation through continuous improvement of deployed systems across hundreds of fulfillment centers in North America and Europe. Our contributions directly impact Amazon's sustainability goals, operational efficiency, and the customer experience for millions of packages shipped daily.

Who We Are
Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.
Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.
Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.
This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.
We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.
If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.
About The Role
We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to build the log replay and scenario execution systems at the core of our simulation platform. In this role, you will take a recorded log from storage, to a replayable test case, to a scored result, and own the execution, determinism, and reporting in between. You will do this across on-road and off-highway programs, and you will own the tooling other engineers use to run scenario suites.
What You’ll Do
Log replay. Build the pipeline that converts recorded logs into replayable test cases, including ingest, indexing, retrieval, and replay of a specific run on demand. Implement open-loop scoring against ground truth and closed-loop replay where the simulated machine is allowed to diverge.
Scenario execution. Build the execution layer that runs a scenario identically every time, including clock control, seed and configuration management, and results traceable to a software version.
Continuous integration. Integrate simulation into CI. Maintain the commit, nightly, and regression workflows, and keep failures attributable.
Metrics and reporting. Implement the pass criteria and metrics a release is judged against, and the reporting that reduces a batch of failing runs to an actionable list.
Scale and cost. Run large batches efficiently, track the cost of a simulation run, and reduce it as volume grows.
Tooling. Build the interfaces, visualizations, and command-line tools that make the platform usable by engineers who did not build it.
Cross-functional work. Work with autonomy and robotics on failure definitions, with bench and hardware-in-the-loop engineering on the path from simulation to bench to vehicle.
What We’re Looking For
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with 5+ years of software engineering experience, or a master's with 3+ years required.
Proficiency in C++ and Python, including the ability to read, navigate, and debug large codebases.
Experience building and operating data or test infrastructure at scale, including pipelines, batch execution, storage and indexing.
Experience with simulation, log replay, or large-scale automated testing for robotics or autonomous vehicles.
Working experience with a robotics middleware and its logging and replay tooling.
Experience handling autonomous driving or robotics sensor data across multiple modalities and timestamps, including camera, LiDAR, and radar.
Practical understanding of determinism and reproducibility, including clock control, seed management, and configuration pinning.
Experience integrating test workloads into continuous integration.
Working fluency with modern AI coding and agentic development tools.
Clear written communication covering design notes and test results.
Willingness to travel occasionally to deployment and test sites.
Ability to work onsite five days a week in San Francisco.
Why join us
At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.
What Else You Need To Know
This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.
The base salary range for this role is
$195,000 - $246,000 per year.
Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.
Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for equity awards.

Flexible Spending Account / Health Savings Account Options
401(k)
Equity
Sick Time, Unlimited Flexible Time Off, and Paid Holidays
Paid Parental Leave
Pre-Tax Commuter Benefit Plan
Team lunch in our SoMa office every Tuesday and Thursday
Benefits Are Subject To Change At The Company's Discretion.
Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

About Ramp
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
About The Role
Over the past few years at Ramp, we've reimagined how businesses manage spend, and the backbone of that vision is Procure-to-Pay. The P2P team builds the systems that connect vendors, invoices, and payments into one seamless, automated flow. It's where billions of dollars move through our platform, and every line of code matters.
We're looking for a backend engineer who loves complex systems, obsesses over correctness, and wants to shape how money moves in modern finance software. You'll help design and scale the infrastructure that powers our payment rails, ensures auditability across products, and unlocks the next wave of AI-driven automation.
It's a chance to work on systems that actually move money, with a team that cares deeply about precision, reliability, and scale. The problems are tough, the stakes are high, and the impact is massive.
What You'll Do
Design and build core P2P systems, from invoice ingestion and approval workflows to payment orchestration and reconciliation logic.
Enable AI agents to classify, validate, and process invoices automatically, reducing manual review and accelerating financial close.
Own backend services that process large volumes of financial events across Bill Pay, Procurement, and Treasury.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Finance, and Data to translate accounting and compliance policies into robust, testable code.
Extend Ramp’s financial ledger to handle new transaction types, international payments, and automated audit trails.
Drive technical excellence around reliability, observability, and data integrity in systems where correctness directly impacts financial reporting.
Continuously improve developer tooling and internal APIs that make P2P data accessible across Ramp’s product ecosystem.
What You Need
3+ years of backend engineering experience, ideally in fintech, payments, or transactional systems.
Proven experience designing and maintaining data-intensive distributed systems with strong consistency and auditability requirements.
Deep knowledge of Python (or a comparable backend language) and SQL.
Comfort building event-driven systems and scaling high-volume, low-latency architectures.
Strong system design and debugging skills; you care about correctness as much as speed.
Ability to work closely with finance, risk, and product stakeholders to translate business rules into software logic.
Passion for building systems that are precise, reliable, and extensible as Ramp scales globally.
Nice to Have
Experience with accounts payable, payments, or reconciliation systems.
Familiarity with accounting or ERP integrations (e.g. NetSuite, QuickBooks, Oracle).
Background in compliance-heavy or regulated domains.
Exposure to AI-driven automation or interest in working with AI/ML teams to build intelligent finance workflows.
Desire to move quickly while maintaining an uncompromising standard for data accuracy and auditability.

At Nerdio, our mission is to simplify the lives of IT professionals and maximize their Microsoft cloud and end user computing investments.
We support organizations of all sizes looking to deploy, manage, and cost-optimize native Microsoft technologies. In fact, our product roadmap is greatly influenced by the regular feedback we receive from having seen companies deploy AVD into production environments several thousand times using Nerdio technology.
Today, Nerdio is used in over 50 countries by more than 15,000 organizations of every size and vertical. We’re committed to delivering exceptional service and support, which starts with identifying and supporting the best staff possible.

The Corporate Development team is Nerdio's internal R&D and AI engineering hub. The Role
Comfy lets people build creative workflows that combine open-source models running on our GPUs with paid APIs from model providers. Every run has a cost. Customers need to understand what they’re spending, and we need to charge accurately as models, prices, and products change.
You’ll own the engineering behind that: how we meter usage, collect payments, manage credits and subscriptions, and protect against financial abuse. You’ll make billing dependable for customers and give the team the tools to launch new pricing models with confidence.
Our billing stack uses Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, Stripe, and Metronome, alongside Python and Kubernetes across the broader platform. You’ll evolve an existing system, work across service boundaries, and take changes from design through production.
What You’ll Do
Capture usage reliably. Build metering for GPU compute and partner model APIs. Handle delayed events, retries, and partial failures so every billable event is recorded once and attributed to the right workspace.
Own the payment lifecycle. Improve checkout, subscriptions, credit top-ups, plan and seat changes, prorations, refunds, and failed-payment recovery. Keep Stripe, Metronome, and our application state consistent when events arrive late or systems fail halfway through.
Reconcile charges, payments, and credits. Build automated checks across usage records, invoices, payments, and credit balances. Detect discrepancies, give operators an audit trail, and recover safely when a payment succeeds but credits never arrive. Own production reliability and turn incidents into lasting improvements.
Make new pricing easier to ship. Build reusable pricing and entitlement systems for individual creators, teams, and enterprise customers. Make changes safe for existing subscribers as we introduce new models, products, and plans.
Limit financial abuse. Improve spend controls and detection of suspicious usage, payment fraud, and credit abuse. Work with Support and Finance on disputes and recovery while keeping checkout and legitimate usage smooth.
Give customers and teammates clear answers. Partner with product and frontend engineers on billing experiences, and build tools that let Support, Sales, and Finance investigate charges and resolve issues safely.
You might be a good fit if you
Have built and operated billing or payments systems in production, with meaningful ownership of usage metering, credits, or consumption-based pricing.
Have integrated Stripe directly and worked through subscription changes, invoices, webhooks, and payment failures beyond the happy path.
Can reason carefully about money across distributed systems: idempotency, concurrent updates, reconciliation, rounding, and recovery after partial failure. You can explain how you found and prevented a real billing error.
Are a strong backend engineer with experience in relational data modeling and reliable APIs. You can learn our stack and work across services to solve a customer problem.
Care about the experience behind the numbers. You can explain technical tradeoffs to Finance, Product, and Support and use their feedback to build better systems.
Take ownership from problem definition through rollout and operation. You use AI development tools effectively and verify their output with the care that systems handling money require.
Bonus if you have
Worked with Metronome, Orb, or a similar metering platform.
Built durable workflows with Temporal.
Billed GPU infrastructure or model APIs, tracked provider costs, or built systems for changing rate cards and per-request margins.
Built spend limits or defenses against card testing, chargeback abuse, or trial and promotional-credit abuse.
Improved international checkout, payment-method coverage, or payment authorization rates.
Used ComfyUI, contributed to open source, or built tools for creative professionals.
About Comfy
Comfy (https://www.comfy.org) is the AI creation engine for visual professionals who demand control over every model, every parameter, and every output. The most powerful workflow engine for visual AI.
Unlike tools that hide everything behind a prompt box, Comfy lets you connect models, processing steps, and outputs on a canvas where every decision is visible and every step is inspectable. It gives you the building blocks to create workflows nobody's imagined yet, and share them with everyone.
What started as an open-source project in 2023 now has 4 million users, 60,000+ community-built nodes, and 150,000+ daily downloads. It's used by artists, filmmakers, game studios, designers, researchers, and VFX houses, including teams at OpenAI, Netflix, Amazon Studios, Ubisoft, EA, and Tencent.
We're a small, intense team in San Francisco. Our team comes from Stability AI and Google, and many contributed to the ComfyUI ecosystem long before working here. Low ego, high ownership. We work hard and demand a lot of each other, but we have fun. Everyone here is building something meaningful that will end up being our life's work.
If this mission excites you and you view yourself as top-tier talent, your future latent self is waiting for you at Comfy.
Check out our Github (https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI) and blog (https://blog.comfy.org). We recently raised $30M at a $500M valuation. The round was led by Craft, with participation from Pace Capital, Chemistry, TruArrow, and others.
Compensation Range: $160K - $240K

Blissway is a startup that simplifies toll collection and dramatically improves highway safety. We are multiple startups in one:
Deep Tech, AI/ML, Hardware, SaaS, and IoT.
For the past five years, we have built a nearly insurmountable technological lead in tolling, an industry that is quietly bigger than football. While our competitors have thousands of employees, we operate with a lean but growing team of less than 30. We’ve stayed under the radar, but our impact is visible on the massive Interstate Highway System connecting every major US metro (except Juneau, AK—sorry, Juneau).
You are a good fit if...
You love the grind: You take ownership and put in the time to meet deadlines. Our recent team survey showed an average of 55 hours/week, with occasional 70+ hour bursts for major releases.
You are detail obsessed: You have experience writing code, designing or building systems that stands up to the unpredictability of the physical world, where the small details are the difference between success and failure.
You are adaptable: We are a lean team. If you only want to work on a "niche thing" or are uncomfortable helping other teams when they need a boost, this isn't the place for you. We expect you to figure out what you need to get stuff done.
You code really well: We mostly use Python and TypeScript, but we don’t care what you’re most proficient in today—as long as you learn fast.
Machine Learning Engineer
The Mission:
You are the engineer who ships the model, not just the one who trains it. At Blissway, we process 11 million images every single day, running detection, segmentation, classification, embeddings, and re-identification across everything in the camera’s frame. You will own the full arc: raw sensor data to production inference, dataset curation to deployment monitoring, cloud to edge. This role is for the engineer who sees a model sitting in a notebook and feels the itch to put it to the test, or in this case, on the road.
The Work
Own the Whole Pipeline: You decide which problems are worth solving, then take them from raw sensor data all the way to production: collection, dataset curation, training, deployment, monitoring, and iteration. We wire it all together and run our own servers, so the pipeline is yours end to end.
Real Hardware in the Real World: This is the part that makes us special. We own the devices in the field. This means any idea you have can actually get built and tested on real roads.
Vision at Real Scale: We process 11 million images every single day, running detection, segmentation, classification, embeddings, and re-identification across everything in the frame: vehicles, license plates, wheels, even lane markings. Beyond images, we have multiple other sensors on the road pulling in different data making the problem space wide open. At this volume, the right model can drastically improve accuracy and cut cost at the same time.
Classical CV to Custom SOTA: Our toolbox spans the full range, from traditional computer vision algorithms to custom-trained state-of-the-art models (detection, segmentation, embeddings, classifiers). You pick the right tool, and when nothing off-the-shelf is good enough, you train your own.
Build the Best Models That Exist: We read the papers, go to the conferences, and hold our work to the current frontier. ML has become essential to Blissway over the past year, and this team is where that bet gets made real.
Edge and Cloud: Most of our compute lives in the cloud where power is effectively unlimited. We're now pushing more inference onto the roadside hardware itself, a completely different problem: the models have to be fast, small, and power-efficient without giving up accuracy. You'll work both sides of that constraint.
Requirements
Experience: 2 to 6 years of software engineering with a focus on machine learning and/or computer vision. We want someone with true end-to-end experience: you've taken models from raw data to production and owned what happens after they ship.
Both Sides: Strong software engineering fundamentals plus hands-on ML. You write production-quality code and you train and debug models. The two overlap, and we want someone comfortable across both.
Full Lifecycle: You've owned models beyond the notebook: trained, deployed, monitored, and iterated in production.
Real CV depth. Experience with modern computer vision and the judgment to know when a classical technique beats a heavy model. You're not reaching for a transformer when a filter will do.
How We Work
We're a small team, which means a more deliberate interview process than you might be used to. In exchange, you get real autonomy from day one, direct access to the people setting technical direction, and work that ships to real roads in weeks, not quarters.
The Process:
We hire software engineers in cohorts. Rather than evaluate candidates on a rolling basis, we collect applications over a two-week window and assess everyone together. This allows us to make fair, considered comparisons and move the strongest candidates through the process efficiently and fairly.
The process has five stages:
Application Review: We (a human) read every application carefully at the close of the approximately two-week window.
Ezra: A brief AI-assisted screening to make sure we're a mutual fit before investing more of your time. Think of this as a way to augment your application.
Screening Interview: A focused conversation to understand your background and motivations.
Technical Interview: A deeper evaluation of your skills and how you think through problems.
Experience Interview: A conversation about how you've worked and what you've built.
Final In-Person: A chance to meet the team and see the work environment firsthand.
We'll be in touch at the close of the application window with next steps.

About Tessera Labs
Tessera Labs is a new category of enterprise software: an AI platform that changes how the world's largest companies run.

Changing any of it is a program measured in years and hundreds of millions of dollars, staffed by armies of consultants, and it fails more often than anyone admits. Most companies have quietly accepted this as the cost of being large.
We don't. Tessera is a transformation engine: a governed, multi-agent platform that understands an enterprise's process, data, and code as one connected system and changes it in weeks rather than years. We're vendor-agnostic by design — SAP, Salesforce, Workday, Oracle, Snowflake, MuleSoft — and tied to none of them.
Two things make this hard, and they're the reason the job is interesting. Governance: every action is logged, traceable, and reversible, because our customers are regulated and these are the systems that close their books. And generality: the platform has to work on landscapes it has never seen, at companies whose complexity is genuinely unique to them.
We sell a product, not a service.
Our people are here to make the product successful, not the other way around. If you've watched enterprise AI companies quietly become consultancies, that distinction is the one to press us on.

Most of the difficulty is not model access. It's an agent reasoning across a landscape with nineteen years of undocumented decisions embedded in it, where one call silently returns a stale schema forty steps into a plan — and the work of making that failure legible, reproducible, and then impossible.
This is not a prototyping role. Everything you build gets pointed at systems a company's quarter close depends on.

Improve agent performance through prompting, context construction, tool-use strategy, and decision logic — and know which of those a given failure calls for.

Manage context deliberately. Enterprise artifacts are enormous and a forty-step run accumulates history fast; deciding what the model sees, what gets compressed, and what gets dropped is a first-class engineering problem here, not a prompt detail.
Use classical ML where it's the right tool. Plenty of the work inside an agent pipeline — routing, ranking, classification, anomaly detection, confidence estimation — is better served by a small supervised model than by another LLM call, and knowing the difference is part of the job.
Build the eval and monitoring layer: task sets drawn from real customer landscapes, regression coverage on every deploy, and alerting that catches a changed schema, a revoked authorization, or a new model version before the customer does.

Our Operating Principles
Extreme Ownership
We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. Craftsmanship

We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.
Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.
First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

Mission
We're looking for someone who can sit with our operations teams and make their day-to-day work easier. You'll start with Managed Services, learn how they actually get things done, and then build the automations and integrations that take the repetitive, manual work off their plate. A lot of the job is scripting, connecting systems, and cleaning up messy processes, with AI tooling and concepts being a big part of it. Position Overview
This is a hands-on role for someone who likes digging into operational problems. Here's what the work looks like:
Embedded work: You'll be part of an operations team, starting with Managed Services. You'll learn their workflows and go after the highest-volume, most painful tasks first.
Automation and integration: You'll write the scripts, jobs, and integrations that connect systems, move data around, and cut out manual steps.
Process improvement: Before automating anything, you'll look for ways to simplify it. Sometimes the best fix is removing a step, not speeding it up.
Building with AI: You'll build AI into the work itself, like an LLM that reads unstructured text or an agent that handles a multi-step task, and you'll use AI tools to build it all faster.
Results: You'll measure where things stand today and track what changes, like time saved and errors avoided.

Process Improvement and Automation
Spend time with an operations team to understand how the work really happens and where automation would make the biggest difference.

Build the scripts, scheduled jobs, API connections, and data pipelines that take manual work off people's plates.

Measure each process before and after so you know what actually improved, then keep refining it.
